subject: community-medicine
title: Incubation Period, Communicable Period, Serial Interval and Herd Immunity

steps.title: Incubation period: entry to first symptoms
steps.tx: The **incubation period** runs from entry of the agent to the first sign or symptom. It reflects generation time of the organism, portal of entry, infective dose and individual immunity. Knowing its range lets investigators work backward from onset to the exposure event, and forward to how long contacts must be watched.
steps.say: Entry to first symptom: that interval does double duty. Work backward from onset to find the exposure; work forward to set contact watching periods. Dose, portal and immunity stretch or shrink it person by person.

steps.title: Using incubation ranges in an outbreak
steps.tx: **Median incubation** anchors food poisoning investigation: cases clustering 12 to 24 hours after a meal point to one family of organisms, while 48 to 72 hours points elsewhere. The earliest and latest cases bound the exposure window. A single case outside the plausible range usually signals a different exposure or secondary spread, not a longer tail.
steps.say: Timing accuses the organism. Cases clustering half a day after a meal suggest one family; three days suggest another. Earliest and latest cases bound the exposure window. Outliers usually mean secondary spread, not statistical tails.

steps.title: Communicable period: when the host infects others
steps.tx: The **communicable period** is the interval during which the agent can pass directly or indirectly from infected person to susceptible person. It may start before symptoms, as in measles catarrh, and outlast them, as in chronic carriage. Isolation durations, school exclusions and return-to-work rules are all built directly on this interval, disease by disease.
steps.say: Infectiousness has its own calendar. It can open before symptoms and close long after them, or never close in chronic carriers. Isolation durations and school exclusions are built directly on this interval, disease by disease.

steps.title: Serial interval and generation time
steps.tx: The **serial interval** runs from onset in a primary case to onset in its secondary case, approximating incubation plus early infectiousness. Generation time runs from infection of the infector to infection of the infectee, unobservable directly. Chains plotted by serial interval reveal generation-by-generation growth, the raw material for judging whether control is bending transmission.
steps.say: Two intervals time the chain. Onset to onset in linked cases is observable; infection to infection is not. Plotting generations by the observable interval shows whether control is bending transmission or merely watching it.

rows: Onset to onset in next case

steps.title: Latent period versus incubation period
steps.tx: The **latent period** runs from infection to infectiousness, while incubation runs from infection to symptoms; their difference decides whether presymptomatic spread occurs. Diseases infectious before symptoms, like influenza and COVID-era respiratory viruses in exam stems, defeat symptom-based isolation. Diseases infectious only after symptoms, like SARS in 2003, surrendered to it.
steps.say: Compare two clocks from infection. One ends at infectiousness, the other at symptoms. Infectious first means presymptomatic spread defeats symptom-based isolation; symptoms first means isolation can actually win.

steps.title: Herd immunity: protection without vaccination
steps.tx: **Herd immunity** is group resistance that protects even unimmunised members when enough of the population is immune, because chains of transmission break for lack of susceptibles. It follows natural infection, active immunisation, or both, and collapses as births and migration dilute the immune share. It never protects against tetanus, whose reservoir is soil, not people.
steps.say: Groups protect their unprotected members when immune density breaks transmission chains. Births and migration dilute it steadily. Tetanus stands outside the concept entirely: soil, not people, carries that reservoir.

steps.title: Herd immunity threshold
steps.tx: The **herd immunity threshold** is the immune proportion above which disease may no longer persist, varying with virulence, vaccine efficacy and population contact patterns. Highly transmissible measles demands a far higher threshold than slower diseases. Serological surveys measure the actual immune share, letting programmes compare reality against the threshold instead of guessing from doses delivered.
steps.say: Persistence has a tipping point. Above the threshold immune share, disease cannot sustain itself; measles sets that bar far higher than slower diseases. Serological surveys measure the real share, replacing dose-count guessing.

steps.title: Active and passive immunity contrasted
steps.tx: **Active immunity** follows infection or vaccination: slow to build, durable, with immunological memory, humoral and cellular arms cooperating. Passive immunity transfers ready antibody: immediate, brief, without memory, as with immunoglobulin after exposure. Combined active-passive protection, as in rabies and hepatitis B post-exposure care, exploits both clocks at once.
steps.say: Two clocks again. Active immunity builds slowly after infection or vaccine and remembers for years. Passive antibody acts immediately and fades within weeks. Post-exposure care for rabies deliberately runs both clocks together.

steps.title: Why some diseases ignore herd logic
steps.tx: **Successful parasitism** describes agents that live in balance with hosts without destroying their habitat, persisting endemically for generations. Where vectors, animal reservoirs or soil maintain the agent, human herd immunity alone cannot eliminate disease. Vector density and animal control then matter as much as vaccine coverage, the closing lesson of this module.
steps.say: Some agents outwait immunity. Balanced parasitism, vectors, animal reservoirs and soil all maintain transmission beyond human immune shares. Elimination then needs vector and reservoir control standing beside vaccine coverage, never behind it.
